options.text: The concave mirror concentrates reflected sunlight into a small bright spot, raising the temperature there.
A convex mirror concentrates sunlight into a small bright hot spot in the same way.
The reflecting surface need not face the Sun for the hot spot to form.
The paper heats because sunlight merely touches the mirror; a small bright spot is not needed.

stem:
The diagram shows Ayesha holding a concave mirror so its reflecting surface faces the Sun. Reflected rays meet on a sheet of paper.

Why can a bright hot spot form on the paper?

teacher.key_rationale: A concave mirror facing the Sun can focus reflected sunlight into a small bright spot hot enough to heat paper. A convex mirror does not concentrate the same way; the reflecting surface must face the Sun; heating is from concentrated energy at the spot, not mere contact with the mirror.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source lens rays into a concave mirror concentrating sunlight onto paper.
